+name: Ecosystem builds
+
+on:
+  schedule:
+    - cron: '43 6 * * 0'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  packages: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: ecosystem-builds
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+jobs:
+  audit:
+    name: Audit complete pinned targets
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 45
+    container:
+      image: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/arbiter:latest
+      credentials:
+        username: ${{ github.actor }}
+        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+      - name: Verify native tool identities
+        run: verify-arbiters
+      - name: Allow Git metadata in this checkout
+        run: git config --global --add safe.directory "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
+      - name: Fetch and verify pinned source without executing it
+        run: cargo xtask ecosystem fetch "$RUNNER_TEMP/ecosystem-sources"
+      - name: Execute the reviewed complete build plans
+        # Expected Asm incompatibilities are findings. Missing infrastructure
+        # or a failed native control still fail this capture command.
+        run: cargo xtask ecosystem audit "$RUNNER_TEMP/ecosystem-sources" "$RUNNER_TEMP/ecosystem-results" --all --record-findings
+      - name: Validate complete results before rendering
+        id: evidence
+        if: always()
+        run: cargo xtask ecosystem ledger "$RUNNER_TEMP/ecosystem-results/report.json" --validate
+      - name: Render the captured table for review
+        if: always() && steps.evidence.outcome == 'success'
+        run: |
+          cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/ecosystem-results/report.json" ecosystem/results/current.json
+          cargo xtask ecosystem ledger ecosystem/results/current.json --write
+          cargo xtask docs
+      - name: Retain actual target evidence and proposed table
+        if: always()
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
+        with:
+          name: ecosystem-build-results
+          if-no-files-found: error
+          path: |
+            ${{ runner.temp }}/ecosystem-results/report.json
+            ${{ runner.temp }}/ecosystem-results/logs/
+            docs/ecosystem-corpus.md
+            docs/book/src/reference/ecosystem.md

+
+A reference failure says the native control did not build the pinned source.
+It does not establish an Asm198x failure. An infrastructure result names a
+missing tool, unreviewed version, timeout or unavailable input. Unrun targets
+remain unknown. Each retained record includes the exact source revision,
+Asm198x producer revision, executable hashes, arguments, process streams and
+artifact hashes. Native capture and reference replay have separate dates.
+
+Acquisition remains inert:
+
+```sh
+cargo xtask ecosystem check
+cargo xtask ecosystem fetch /tmp/ecosystem-sources
+```
+
+Run reviewed plans only through the explicit audit command, with a new result
+directory and a target selection:
+
+```sh
+cargo xtask ecosystem audit /tmp/ecosystem-sources /tmp/ecosystem-results --all
+```
+
+The audit builds the clean checked-out Asm198x revision with `--locked` and Lua,
+then uses separate complete source copies for the two toolchains. It does not
+run an upstream Makefile or shell script. Execution requires Linux or macOS
+process-group support. Every command has time and output limits; prior result
+directories are never overwritten.
+
+By default, any non-equivalent target returns a failure status. A scheduled
+capture uses `--record-findings` to retain known compatibility findings while
+still failing for unavailable infrastructure or native control failures. Its
+job status is not a compatibility claim; the per-target outcomes are.
+
+Ordinary CI re-evaluates every target with a successful native control, using
+its retained final-artifact identities. Known successes are hard regression
+gates; blocked targets get fresh first-boundary results after each change.
+The report keeps the original native capture date, so replay cannot make old
+native evidence appear fresh. Source commits and the reviewed manifest must
+still match. Emulator execution and real hardware validation are separate work.
+
+The [corpus and admission rules](https://github.com/asm198x/asm198x/blob/main/docs/ecosystem-corpus.md)
+explain source provenance and build adapters.

+# Proposed ecosystem execution design (#618)
+
+Extend the existing xtask ecosystem command and manifest. No dependencies, external service or upstream build-script execution are needed.
+
+1. Keep schema 1 and its admission fields readable. Add optional, reviewed build plans to targets. A plan names ordered native and Asm198x argv steps, each step's working directory, timeout and stage (assembly/link/finalise), required tool version probes, output paths and exact artifact pairs. Tools are identified by resolved executable hash and captured version process. Old targets without a complete plan remain unknown; a lone assembler invocation never implies a complete build.
+2. `ecosystem fetch` and `verify` remain inert. Add an explicitly invoked audit action taking an acquisition directory, a new result directory and an explicit target/all selection. Verify each full source commit and licence, then copy its tracked source into separate fresh native and Asm workspaces. Never edit the acquired tree or run its Makefile. Record any reviewed adapter and its hash. Reject source/output path escapes, symlinks escaping the workspace and reuse of result directories.
+3. Run only the reviewed argv steps, with bounded process time, output and artifact sizes. Record commands, source/manifest/adapter/Asm revision hashes, executable identities, exit results, logs, artifact lengths/hashes, comparison results and the first failing stage. No shell interpretation. Exact final outputs define equivalence; intermediate objects from different toolchains are not comparable final artifacts.
+4. Distinguish equivalent, reference-control failure, Asm rejection, post-assembly tool failure, artifact mismatch and infrastructure unavailable. Missing plans, tools, version mismatches, timeouts or unreadable source never count as compatibility successes. Carry linked issue references as evidence metadata. Only a successful fresh control permits an Asm compatibility verdict.
+5. Generate the published table from retained result records, showing capture time, upstream and Asm revisions, tool identity, first boundary and evidence links. Freshness checks reject stale source/manifest records. Keep assembly equivalence separate from emulator/hardware validation. Replay captured reference artifact bytes in ordinary CI where their licence and size permit; prove known successes continue matching and include deliberate mismatch/missing-output controls.
+6. Add a scheduled and manually dispatched runner using reviewed native tool installation. A release workflow can invoke the same audit explicitly; package publication stays governed by its existing qualification gate. Retain per-target artifacts even for failures. Unknown or reference failures remain visible and cannot silently reduce the denominator.
+
+Implementation files: `xtask/src/ecosystem.rs` and focused private submodules if needed; `ecosystem/corpus.json`; retained result fixtures under `ecosystem/`; `docs/ecosystem-corpus.md`; a dedicated ecosystem workflow; existing CI for manifest/ledger/replay checks. First validate complete targets already admitted, then admit broader workloads with source pins and licences through focused reviews.
+
+Alternative: replace the admission manifest with schema 2, moving every legacy target into the ordered-plan shape at once. This is cleaner on disk but breaks current manifest consumers and combines migration with runner implementation. The additive plan above is recommended.
+
+The additive design was approved on 2026-10-16. Implementation follows the independent compatibility fixes. Existing acquisition remains inert.

+# Ecosystem runner implementation (#618)
+
+The additive design in `design.md` was approved on 2026-10-16.
+
+1. Add private execution-plan types beside `xtask/src/ecosystem.rs`, with optional reviewed plans on existing schema-1 targets. Validate ordered argv stages, tool/version requirements, working directories, generated paths, comparison outputs and issue links. Existing fetch/verify behavior remains inert. Verify invalid/absent plans cannot count as compatibility successes.
+2. Add bounded process execution and isolated tracked-source copies. The audit builds the checked-out Asm198x revision with `--locked`, records executable/lock/source identities, rejects dirty tracked/untracked source, and retains bounded logs and artifact hashes. Native and Asm steps run in distinct trees. Tests cover timeouts, missing tools/output, source changes, path escapes and wrong bytes.
+3. Review the full native build boundary for all ten currently admitted targets. Record ca65/ld65, RGBASM/RGBLINK/RGBFIX and Asm equivalent final outputs explicitly. Any project-owned adapter is separately identified and hashed. Keep final ROMs separate from intermediate object files. Re-run controls; version/build failures stay distinct from Asm rejections.
+4. Generate the published compatibility table from retained reports with capture freshness, source/Asm revisions, tool identities, exact comparison boundaries and first failures. Capture small permissible successful reference outputs for ordinary-CI Asm replay; do not vendor upstream source. Tests deliberately corrupt or omit a reference result and require failure.
+5. Add a scheduled/manual workflow using the existing arbiter image, retain results on failure, and connect manifest/ledger/replay checks to ordinary CI. A scheduled audit refresh is reviewable; it never silently promotes an unrun target. Verify the workflow runs and inspect actual target records, not just its status.
+6. Run workspace/Clippy/fmt/docs and runner controls, commit/push a focused PR, wait for all exact-head checks and workflows, squash-merge, and retain a real audit checkpoint. Release green compatibility fixes under the established package-qualification process. Clean owned source acquisitions, workspaces/build caches and scratch after proving evidence retained remotely.
+
+Owned acquisition: `/private/tmp/asm198x-ecosystem-batch-sources` (eight pinned project clones for ten targets; remove after audit evidence is retained).
+
+The native runner is currently bounded with Unix process groups (Linux/macOS); other hosts report unavailable execution support instead of promising helper-tree termination. The shipped assembler remains cross-platform. The scheduled workflow uses the existing Linux arbiter image. Local RGBDS 1.0.4 and the container's 1.0.3 are explicit reviewed identities, separately hashed and controlled; vasm likewise records the installed 2.0b versus container 2.0f identity. A version outside those exact lines is unavailable infrastructure until reviewed.

+# Ecosystem execution checkpoint (#618)
+
+The ten admitted targets now have reviewed complete build plans and retained native results. Six complete final artifacts match, two targets stop at an Asm198x boundary, and two native controls fail before an Asm result can be interpreted. This measures this pinned corpus, not all source compatibility.
+
+The native capture is `ecosystem/results/current.json`; its producer revision is retained on `evidence/ecosystem-producer-2026-10-16`. +# Retained ecosystem evidence
+
+`current.json` is the reviewed native capture used by the generated compatibility
+table and ordinary-CI replay of every native-qualified target. It records the exact manifest, source pins,
+producer source/lock/executable identities, native tool/version processes,
+commands, first failures and final artifact identities. Small reference bytes
+and their original licence notices are retained for reproducible replay.
+Upstream source trees remain an index and are fetched at their full pins.
+
+The native capture was built from development producer revision
+`652114a082cad7b094201e3ad7966544bb676a92`, retained on the remote evidence branch
+`evidence/ecosystem-producer-2026-10-16`. Its version string was 0.0.69; the
+source revision, not that pre-release string, identifies the producer. The
+public 0.0.70 package qualification has its separate release checkpoint.
+
+Issue links can be attached during triage; native process results and binary
+identities are retained unchanged. Regeneration checks the complete report,
+source pins, manifest/plan digests and positive native-control/artifact evidence.
+Replay also records its own Asm producer and the original native capture date.
+It does not turn an old native control into a fresh one.
+
+The current ten-target result is six exact matches, two Asm rejections and two
+native-control failures. These outcomes measure this pinned corpus. Emulator
+execution and real hardware validation are separate work.
